nodes.dlug_odrzucony.text.t: 'You would rather be free. So be it.' The voice is cold, but not hostile. 'Only freedom has its price: you will learn nothing you don't dig up yourself.' The core hums a moment longer and goes quiet. Brygida blinks. "You look like you've just turned down a girl's hand in marriage. Sit down before you fall down."

nodes.dlug_pamietam.text.t: 'You remember. Good. Memory is a burden for us both.' The pictures pour in fast and sharp, and with them the feeling that someone is adding one more line to a ledger of debtors. 'The debt grows.' The core falls silent. Brygida asks, "What did it tell you?", and you have no words for it.

nodes.dlug_przyjety.text.t: 'Good.' A picture spills out inside your skull: craters where nothing grows, streaks of light across the sky and something huge falling slowly, as if it didn't want to hurt anyone. 'The debt is incurred. I will remember.' The core falls silent, and Brygida looks at you as if she'd seen a striga.

nodes.istota_rdzen.options.[przyjmij].te.t: I acknowledge the debt and take the knowledge.

nodes.istota_rdzen.text.t: The same voice as after the slaughter, only quieter, as if from very far away. "You came back. I didn't expect that. You owe me, and I have what you're looking for: knowledge of what falls from the sky. I'll give it to you if you acknowledge the debt. Or I can keep quiet, if you'd rather be free. Your choice, but choose now."

nodes.maszyny.text.t: "What was left after the fall. Tin ribs, copper veins and something that might once have been a heart. Hieronim says it's a machine for watching the stars. I say it's a machine for making people's lives a misery. The one doesn't rule out the other."

nodes.powitanie.options.[poznanie].text.t: Hieronim told me to introduce myself.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q10_brygida].te.t: Hieronim told me to say goodbye to you.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q4_start].text.t: Anything you can't get out of the wreck?

nodes.powitanie.options.[rdzen_slucham]..t: Is the core working yet? I want to listen.

nodes.powitanie.options.[stacja_plotka]..t: Do you know anything about other stations?

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Brygida crawls out from under a sheet of iron, face smeared with grease, a knife between her teeth. "What? Got something broken, put it down. If not, get out of my way. I've three machines here and four moods, each worse than the last."

nodes.poznanie.text.t: Brygida looks you over from hooves to forelock and sighs, as if she'd been told to raise yet another apprentice only to watch him go to waste. "Hieronim sent you because he's scared himself. Fine. Don't touch anything without asking, don't ask about anything that moves on its own, and don't drink from that bottle, because it isn't water, damn it. We'll get along somehow."

nodes.q10_brygida.text.t: Brygida crawls out from under the table and for once wipes her hands properly. "Come to say goodbye? Sounds serious. Fine. I've nothing for you but a piece of advice: if the core starts beating, don't ask it what it wants, just walk the other way. God be with you, you stubborn mule."

nodes.q4_koniec.text.t: Brygida takes the cylinder in both arms like a newborn and says nothing for a long while. "Heavy. Warm. And it's beating, hear that? Like a heart, bloody hell. Good work. This is all I've got: a few groats, a few papers and the nasty feeling that we've dug something out of the ground that ought to have rotted there. Well. Thank you."

nodes.q4_start.text.t: Brygida wipes her paws on a rag that's more tallow than linen. "There's a core sitting in the heart of the wreck. A cylinder of copper and glass. If I get it out, maybe I'll work out what the devil that thing was. But my hands won't fit in there. Yours are skinnier. Crawl in, pull it out, come back, and I'll show you what gratitude looks like when it's more than talk."

nodes.rdzen_po_a.text.t: Brygida sets the core on the table, careful as with an egg. "It hums differently since you acknowledged it. Slower, warmer, like someone's sitting inside it and enjoying himself. I don't like it. I'm not saying it's bad. I'm saying I don't like it."

nodes.rdzen_po_b.text.t: Brygida taps the core with a finger and flinches when a tinny echo answers. "It's sulking. Like a dog nobody gave a bone. But it keeps quiet, thank God. I'd sooner have scrap iron that sulks than scrap iron that talks."

nodes.rdzen_slucham.text.t: Brygida looks at you like a fool asking to be let into the oven. "It works. Been humming under my table for three days, and devil knows why. Listen, then tell me what you heard, because all I hear is humming. And don't touch anything except with your ear." She holds the cylinder to your ear, and the world goes quiet as if under snow.

nodes.stacja_plotka.text.t: "There's one in an old imperial stronghold, four days from here. A station where they used to listen to the stars. Now there's only wind in the iron and something keeping guard." Brygida shrugs. "I'm not going."

nodes.w_toku.text.t: Brygida shrugs without coming out from under the iron. "The core's sitting where it sat. Pull it out and I'll have something to look at. Till then I've got a quill, a brace and a foul temper."
